claims.text: The FeNiCrCoCu coating undergoes a temperature-induced transition from dislocation-mediated plasticity to rapid lattice disordering and localized shear banding.
At 300 K, lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening suppress dislocation mobility in FeNiCrCoCu.
Suppressed dislocation mobility maintains the coating's high elastic modulus and stable wear resistance at 300 K.
Increasing temperature thermally activates dislocation glide by reducing the Peierls barrier.
At a critical temperature, thermal energy overcomes ordering or short-range-order stability in FeNiCrCoCu and produces a disordered state.
Disordering and thermo-plastic shear-band instability cause a rapid loss of strain-hardening capacity.
Dislocation density initially rises with temperature and subsequently saturates or decreases through dynamic recovery and amorphous-like shear-band formation.
The FeNiCrCoCu coating is likely nanocrystalline or fine-grained and contains high lattice distortion and possible short-range order.
Temperature evolution of the deformation structure includes a reduction in stacking-fault energy.
Elevated temperature and sliding deformation produce shear bands containing localized atomic disorder, amorphization, or loss of short-range order.
High-strain, high-temperature compression of Al0.1CrCoFeNi provides an analogy for shear-induced disordering in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The Cu matrix may dissipate heat or act as a sink for defects.
Intrinsic instability of the FeNiCrCoCu coating dominates the wear failure despite the presence of the Cu matrix.
Wear resistance remains stable up to a critical temperature of approximately 600–700 K.
Above the critical temperature, wear depth increases by more than one order of magnitude because of shear banding and lattice disordering.
Hardness and elastic modulus drop suddenly above the critical temperature.
Stacking-fault structures become unstable and dissolve or transform into amorphous regions inside shear bands above the transition.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to a fully amorphous coating or when melting or substantial oxidation controls failure.

contradictions.description: The mediator specifies a reduction in stacking-fault energy, which ordinarily stabilizes and promotes stacking faults, while the predicted outcome says stacking faults become unstable and dissolve. No later increase in stacking-fault energy or other explanation reconciling these statements is supplied.

The mechanism asserts that intrinsic coating instability dominates over Cu-matrix effects, while the uncertainty field states that the matrix influence on heat dissipation and defect annihilation is unknown.
